recipes.name: Turkey Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 2 cups shredded Cheddar-Monterey Jack cheese blend
1 tablespoon oil, divided, or more as needed

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Pour enchilada sauce into a bowl.
Combine Cheddar-Jack cheese, onion, and black olives in a small bowl.

Brush a small skillet with enough oil to coat a tortilla, and heat over low heat. Cook tortilla in hot oil until softened, 15 to 30 seconds per side. Remove and dip in enchilada sauce to coat, then place on a plate.
Place some turkey and some cheese mixture in the center of the tortilla, roll up, and place it in the prepared baking dish.
Repeat Steps 4 and 5, using more oil as needed, to form and roll 11 more enchiladas; they should cover the bottom of the baking dish. Spread enchilada sauce over the enchiladas to cover.
Repeat Steps 4 and 5 to form, roll, and place remaining 12 enchiladas.
Spread remaining sauce over top and sprinkle with remaining cheese mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until heated through and cheese is melted, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Turkey Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: These turkey enchiladas are easy to make with leftover turkey, enchilada sauce, and lots of cheese for a tasty post-Thanksgiving meal.

review.reviewBody: My family and I actually had a contest who could make the best leftover turkey, and I won with this recipe. I did make a few changes...I add 1/2 cup sour cream to the cheese and onion mixture, I took someone's advice and cooked the turkey on medium heat in water and taco seasoning, I also added a small can of green chiles to the cheese mixture, which I sauteed with the onions before adding to the enchiladas. I also used corn tortillas. These were delicious!

My husband goes for the ham at our Thanksgiving Table as he's not a turkey fan. After trying this leftover turkey recipe, however, he's calling me Queen of the Kitchen!i made modifications based on others' reports: Pan Size: 11x5; Sauce: 1 can; Meat: 3 cups turkey simmered in 1 cup chicken broth and 1/2 pkg. taco seasoning; Cheese layer: 12 oz. sour cream, 2 cups cheese of choice, 1 4 oz. can green chilies; tortilla layer: corn tortillas, shredded cheese with habanero peppers. I created 2 complete layers---sauce, tortillas, cheesy layer, turkey layer and habanero cheese---and ended with a tortilla and habanero cheese layer. To keep the top from drying out, I poured about 1/3 cup of the turkey-taco broth over the final tortilla layer. Baked covered for 25 minutes and uncovered for 10 minutes. Absolutely incredible!

I left out the black olives because I'm the only one who likes them in a recipe. I also made them like tacos instead of rolled up. Still stacked them two high. Topped off the dish with Stokes Green Chili Sauce with Pork, which gave it the 5-stars rating. Without the Stokes, it would have been a 4.8. :-)

I made this last year and added refried beans to the mix. 
This year I added 1 cup of sour creme and a 2 ounce can of mild green chili to the cheese mixture. Shredded the turkey and simmered with 1 tbsp butter and the onions in 3 cups of water and taco seasoning. Simmered until the onions were clear. Spooned the meat and onion mixture onto the enchiladas, then a spoon of the cheese mixture. I can use the broth later too. Adding beans would of been good this year.

I should’ve read some of the comments and reviews before making this dish. The onions should be sautéed before being mixed with the cheese. I was a little confused about how to build the dish. 24 tortillas is a lot. 12 of them covered the bottom of baking dish. I wound up building a separate dish and putting it in the freezer for later. Also I used a large can of enchilada sauce instead of the smaller, 19 oz can. Without that, I think it would’ve been dry. Next time I make this dish I will utilize some of the suggestions from others who have tried and improved upon this recipe.
This was very good and will make again. I do let the tortillas drain on paper towels before dipping in sauce. I add a can of chopped green chiles. It's a great use of leftover smoked turkey!

This was yummy way to use last of turkey leftovers. I cooked the onions and green chillies together and added the chopped turkey, taco seasoning & half cup of sour cream. Then filled each tortilla with the turkey mixture, cheese & topped with sauce, cheese & olives. Served with fresh guacamole and beans it was a great Sunday night football meal.

I used some of the suggestions on the reviews (such as putting some of the sauce on the bottom of the baking pan instead of dredging the tortillas) and it turned out great. I did modify it to the point that it may as well be a different recipe, though... I sauteed my veggies first and added one roma tomato, one jalapeno, and half a 6 oz can of olives, chopped - a healthy pinch of paprika, cumin, and chili powder - a smidge of salsa, and sauteed all that with the turkey and mixed in the cheese once off the heat (All 2 cups worth). I also topped the enchiladas with a little extra cheddar and the last half of the can of olives. For anyone complaining about the blandness of this recipe, try it this way and your taste buds will be dancing in delight!

I thought this was a good recipe - I used it as inspiration. I started with ground turkey, and browned it with 1/2 c of onion, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp each paprika and chili powder and 1/4 tsp black pepper and some salt. Once it was browned I added some green enchilada sauce (canned) and then rolled the mixture in 10 white corn tortillas, topping with more enchilada sauce and a little bit of cheese. Baked 20 minutes at 350 and they were yummy.

I had to make some changes to use what I had on hand and tried to incorporate some of the comments. I gave the turkey, olives, sauteed onion, and cheese (1/2 mexican blend and 1/2 pepperjack) a whirl in my food processor with 1/2 cup of water and a few Tblsp of taco seasoning. I just pulsed it -- not a puree! Then I used 2 cans of enchilada sauce, one on the bottom of the pan and one over the top of the rolled enchiladas. I did not have time to heat/dip the tortilla shells. I forgot to add more cheese to the top. Good flavor. Served with sour cream and lettuce. I think some black beans would've been good, too. For the turkey, I used a leftover rotisserie turkey breast. Good flavor, but I wanted some more zip. Maybe some green onions on top when I heat up my leftovers?

This sounds like an awesome recipe as written and I really wanted to try it. That being said, I was too burned out on cooking after Thanksgiving to stand there and individually heat and roll all of those enchiladas so I made some adjustments. Instead, I used the shells to make an enchilada lasagna. For the filling, I added 1 cup of both sour cream & green chilies to the original recipe. I didn't bother to heat the shells since I wasn't rolling them. I put sauce in the bottom of a 13X9 pan, then a layer of 6 overlapping shells, more sauce to cover the shells, 1/2 the filling, repeat to end with shells and sauce on top. I topped it with more cheese and baked for 30 minutes at 375. Lazy, but delicious.
This was easy to make. I did make one change. I omitted the olives. I didn’t have any. We all enjoyed it. I will definitely make it again.
Fantastic use of leftover turkey! I grated pepper jack and extra sharp cheese to give it a little more zip. I would have enjoyed more sauce and increase it next time.
I used green sauce and 2 jalapeños
The receipe is easy. I used Flour Tortillas so I could use all my turkey. Used Homemade Enchilada Sauce. So I already know these things rock. Yummy

Just made this for tailgating last night a big hit. Also made Spanish rice original from this site . the others in our group always bug me till I make the rice every year. GO GRIZ on to the national Championship
Delious! I had a turkey that need to be eaten. It was a hit. I did boil the turkey in water and spices for a little bit to soften.

Family liked these enchiladas, but it seems hard to mess up this recipe. I left out a few ingredients because my family doesn't like olives or onions. The corn tortillas should be warm to keep them from tearing.
